visual_anatomy.title: A broad two-line instructional headline uses two lavender rough-display tags for the key input and intended outcome, then adds a single-line comment call to action.
visual_anatomy.layout: Five equal-width tinted columns progress from one to five-plus ingredients. Each column holds four small template thumbnails, showing different diagram families that can accommodate that amount of input.
visual_anatomy.reading_order: Headline and call to action → column heading for ingredient count → scan the four selectable mini-templates inside that column → compare across columns as input complexity grows.
visual_anatomy.typography: Large light sans title, rough-display tag words, small column headings, and compact template names above each miniature.
visual_anatomy.colour: Pale lavender, pink, aqua, blue, and coral column fields distinguish increasing input groups; miniature diagrams reuse matching but muted treatments.
visual_anatomy.surface: Flat library/index page with finely outlined template thumbnails, small pale depth on inner cards, and a strong white margin around the five-column catalogue.
visual_anatomy.modules: Five ingredient-count columns and twenty miniature diagrams, each acting as a visual affordance rather than a complete worked example.
visual_anatomy.density: High but deliberately browseable: column membership narrows selection before the reader inspects any individual template.

transferable_mechanism.reader_job: Choose a visual form based on the amount and relationship of the material before designing the finished piece.
transferable_mechanism.argument_shape: Input-complexity index crossing ingredient count with diagram-family options.
transferable_mechanism.mechanism: Organise a bounded visual repertoire by a simple selection criterion, then show small distinguishable previews so the reader can route toward an appropriate grammar without reading a long manual.
transferable_mechanism.use_condition: Use when the index is a genuine selection aid with a clear selection variable and each preview represents a materially different visual grammar, not merely a recoloured template.
